```{python}
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
```

```{python}
# Join pace intensity from paces_df into training_df for a given pace column.
# pace_col: column in df holding the pace zone name (e.g. 'speed_rep_pace_name')
# result_col: name for the new intensity column added to df
def merge_intensity(df, pace_col, result_col):
    lookup = paces_df[['name', 'intensity']].rename(columns={'name': pace_col, 'intensity': result_col})
    return pd.merge(df, lookup, on=pace_col, how='left')

# Line chart with distance on the left y-axis and intensity on the right y-axis.
def dual_axis_plot(weeks, primary_y, secondary_y, title, primary_label, secondary_label):
    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))

    ax1.plot(weeks, primary_y, marker='o', color='green', label=primary_label)
    ax1.set_title(title)
    ax1.set_xlabel('Week')
    ax1.set_ylabel(primary_label, color='green')
    ax1.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='green')
    ax1.grid(True)

    ax2 = ax1.twinx()
    ax2.plot(weeks, secondary_y, marker='x', color='red', linestyle='--', label=secondary_label)
    ax2.set_ylabel(secondary_label, color='red')
    ax2.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='red')

    handles = [
        plt.Line2D([0], [0], color='green', marker='o', label=primary_label),
        plt.Line2D([0], [0], color='red', marker='x', linestyle='--', label=secondary_label),
    ]
    ax1.legend(handles=handles, loc='upper left')
    plt.xticks(weeks)
    plt.show()
```

## Data

`paces_df` defines the six pace zones and their ordinal intensity (1 = Easy → 6 = Mile pace). That intensity scale is the key derived variable joined into the weekly training data for visualization.

```{python}
paces_df = pd.read_csv('data/paces.csv')
training_df = pd.read_csv('data/training.csv')

paces_df
```

```{python}
training_df
```

## Feature Engineering

Merge pace intensity into `training_df` for both the speed session and the long run, then compute total speed workout volume for the week.

```{python}
training_df = merge_intensity(training_df, 'speed_rep_pace_name', 'speed_intensity')
training_df = merge_intensity(training_df, 'long_run_pace_name', 'long_run_intensity')

# Easy long runs have no structured pace target — treat their intensity as 0
training_df['long_run_intensity'] = training_df['long_run_intensity'].fillna(0)

# Total structured speed volume per week: number of reps × distance per rep
training_df['speed_total_workout_distance'] = training_df['n_speed_reps'] * training_df['speed_rep_distance (mi)']

training_df.head()
```

## Plots

The plots below overlay intensity on a secondary y-axis so volume and effort level can be read together on the same chart.

```{python}
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(training_df['week'], training_df['total_mileage'], marker='o', color='blue', label='Total Mileage')
plt.plot(training_df['week'], training_df['long_run_distance (mi)'], marker='x', color='red', label='Long Run Distance')
plt.title('Total Mileage and Long Run Distance by Week')
plt.xlabel('Week')
plt.ylabel('Distance (miles)')
plt.grid(True)
plt.xticks(training_df['week'])
plt.legend()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
dual_axis_plot(
    weeks=training_df['week'],
    primary_y=training_df['speed_total_workout_distance'],
    secondary_y=training_df['speed_intensity'],
    title='Speed Session Volume and Pace Intensity by Week',
    primary_label='Speed Total Workout Distance (miles)',
    secondary_label='Pace Intensity',
)
```

```{python}
dual_axis_plot(
    weeks=training_df['week'],
    primary_y=training_df['long_run_speed_pace_distance (mi)'],
    secondary_y=training_df['long_run_intensity'],
    title='Long Run Speed Pace Distance and Intensity by Week',
    primary_label='Long Run Speed Pace Distance (mi)',
    secondary_label='Long Run Pace Intensity',
)
```
